items.prompt: Reverse the digits of a signed 32-bit integer; return 0 if the result overflows.
items.why: A digit loop (% 10, // 10) with an explicit 32-bit range check. Strings work, but the follow-up forbids them and the overflow check is the point.

items.prompt: Count the primes less than n = 5,000,000.
items.why: Many primality facts up to n → Sieve of Eratosthenes, O(n log log n). Trial division per number is far slower.

items.prompt: Compute floor(sqrt(x)) for x up to 2^31 − 1 without a sqrt function.
items.why: Monotone condition mid·mid ≤ x → binary search on the answer, O(log x).

items.prompt: A non-negative integer is stored as an array of digits (most significant first). Add one to it.
items.why: Grade-school addition from the last digit with a carry; the 999 → 1000 case grows the array.

items.prompt: Two traffic lights cycle every a and b seconds and both turn green at t = 0. When do they next turn green together?
items.why: That's lcm(a, b) = a / gcd(a, b) · b, with gcd from Euclid in O(log min(a, b)).

items.prompt: Given 10^5 points on a grid, find the largest Manhattan distance |x1 − x2| + |y1 − y2| between any two of them.
items.why: Expand the absolute values into sign cases: the answer is max(max(x+y) − min(x+y), max(x−y) − min(x−y)). O(n) instead of O(n²).

items.prompt: Every number in the array appears twice except one. Find the single one with O(1) extra space.
items.why: Pairs cancel under XOR → one running XOR. The sum trick 2·sum(set) − sum needs a set, so O(n) space.

items.prompt: Repeatedly replace n by the sum of the squares of its digits. Decide whether you eventually reach 1 or loop forever.
items.why: The digit math is easy; the real question is cycle detection on the sequence → Floyd's slow/fast pointers with O(1) space.
